title: Surge topology & handoff checklist for emergency GPU capacity
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact operational guide for handling unplanned demand surges that require immediate expansion of GPU inference capacity across regions. Focus is practical: topology options, quick math for buffer decisions, exact handoff steps for oncall engineers, and a short postmortem checklist.

Scope:
- Applies to Hosted and Dedicated pool surge handling (private deployments follow private runbooks).
- Only covers immediate (0–3h) actions to stabilize customer traffic and ensure graceful degradation.
- Does NOT replace the longer-term capacity planning spreadsheet (see linked artifacts).

Key definitions (quick):
- Baseline QPS: average inference requests per second over prior 1h.
- Token-rate factor: avg model tokens produced per request (including prompt + completion).
- Sustained headroom target: target buffer above baseline to absorb spikes without autoscale churn. Default = 35%.
- Surge window: length of time we expect elevated demand. Short < 30m, Medium 30–180m, Long > 3h.

Assumptions used in quick math (adjust per model/region):
- avg tokens per req = 75 tokens
- avg token throughput per GPU (8x A100 80GB equivalent) = 10k tokens/sec (observed for gen models at p50 latency targets)
- GPU pool usable efficiency = 0.82 (loss due to batching/overhead)
- baseline_qps e.g., us-west-1 = 420 qps

Quick capacity calc (one-line):
- tokens_per_sec = baseline_qps * tokens_per_req
- tokens_capacity_per_gpu = token_throughput_per_gpu * usable_efficiency
- gpus_needed = ceil( (tokens_per_sec * (1 + headroom)) / tokens_capacity_per_gpu )

Example (us-west-1):
- tokens_per_sec = 420 * 75 = 31,500 t/s
- tokens_capacity_per_gpu = 10,000 * 0.82 = 8,200 t/s
- headroom = 0.35 -> required = 31,500 * 1.35 = 42,525 t/s
- gpus_needed = ceil(42,525 / 8,200) = 6 GPUs (round up and ensure pooling alignment)

Topology options (ranked by speed of recovery):
1) Local-burst (fastest): add GPUs to same region pool (if spare GPUs available in region). Pros: minimal latency impact. Cons: requires local spare inventory.
2) Cross-region warm-failover (recommended when local capacity < needed): shift non-critical traffic to nearest warm region with capacity. Pros: uses existing warm reserves. Cons: increased latency for shifted requests.
3) Model-fallback to smaller variant (software option): route degraded quality to lower-size model serving more throughput. Pros: avoids infra churn. Cons: quality impact needs product signoff.
4) Throttle-and-prioritize (controlled degradation): reduce low-priority routes, protect critical users. Pros: immediate; Cons: customer impact.

Spare inventory policy (operational):
- Each primary region should maintain a float of spare GPUs equivalent to 20% of steady-state pool or minimum of 4 GPUs, whichever is higher.
- Edge regions (APAC smaller footprints) min spare = 2 GPUs.
- Dedicated customer pools may opt-out; for those we track reserve-on-demand contracts.

Emergency handoff checklist (oncall prescriptive):
1) Triage (0–5 min):
   - Confirm spike with dashboards (Console > per-model latency & token burn).
   - Notify #infra-ops and set channel topic to INCIDENT: GPU-SURGE.
   - Snapshot baseline QPS and which model(s) are hot (copy from console).
2) Execute quick calc (5–10 min):
   - Run quick capacity calc in the incident template (copy into slack).
   - Check regional spare inventory (infra inventory dashboard).
3) Choose topology path (10–15 min):
   - If local spare >= needed -> Local-burst (goto step 4a).
   - If not, check warm pool in neighbor region -> Warm-failover (goto 4b).
   - If neither, consider model-fallback or throttle (goto 4c).
4a) Local-burst steps (if spare available):
   - Use infra-scripts: ./scale-pool --region <REG> --add-gpus <N> --reason "INCIDENT GPU SURGE"
   - Watch autoscale logs and token utilization. Verify p95 latency returns to SLO within 5–10 min.
   - If scale fails, escalate to oncall infra-sre (pager) and switch to warm-failover.
4b) Cross-region warm-failover steps:
   - Update routing policy: increase weight for target region by X% (where X equals computed spillover qps fraction).
   - Command (example): ./routing-control shift-weight --from us-west-1 --to us-east-1 --pct 35 --dry-run=false
   - Monitor latency and error rates; keep communications updated on channel every 5 minutes.
4c) Software mitigations and throttles:
   - Apply route-level throttles for non-paying/demo traffic: ./rate-limit update --route /demo --limit 50rps
   - If configured, switch model variant for specific routes via feature-flag: ff toggle model-fallback.<route>=on

Verification & rollback criteria:
- Success: p95 latency within SLO and error-rate <= 0.5% for 2 consecutive 5-min windows.
- If latency not improving or error-rate rises -> rollback change (routing or scale) and escalate to pager chain.

Escalation matrix (fast):
- Oncall infra -> infra-sre lead -> platform-eng manager -> Head of SRE (each 10 minutes if unresolved). Contact numbers in ops vault.

Post-incident quick notes (first 24h):
- Capture incident timeline including decisions and commands used.
- Estimate total GPU-hours used for surge and annotate on incident ticket (JIRA-OPS-1298).
- Decide if we need to move more inventory to the affected region (follow longer-term capacity runbook).

Retrospective prompts (to fill after stability):
- Was headroom assumption (35%) sufficient? Suggest new headroom: ___%
- Did topology choice minimize customer impact?
- Any tooling gaps (routing-control, inventory dashboard) that slowed action?

Quick reference table (copy into chat when incident starts):
Region | baseline_qps | tokens/s | tokens/gpu | headroom | gpus_needed
us-west-1 | 420 | 31,500 | 8,200 | 35% | 6
us-east-1 | 280 | 21,000 | 8,200 | 35% | 4
apac-sg  | 120 | 9,000  | 8,200 | 50% | 2 (note: APAC uses higher headroom policy)

Notes & known limitations:
- Token throughput per GPU varies significantly by model and sequence length; when unsure, run quick perf test in staging with same model and sample prompt cohort.
- Warm-failover increases customer latency; product teams should sign off on pre-approved spill policies for critical routes.

Action items (owners):
- Sophie: reconcile spare GPU inventory dashboard with cloud provider reservations (due 2026-06-10).
- Evan: add a one-click routing rollback command to routing-control (PR open ref in linked artifacts).
- Asha: run two simulated surge drills in the next quarter and document time-to-stabilize.

If you are oncall and stuck: tag @infra-sre-lead in #infra-ops and attach the incident checklist from this doc.
